{"findings": [
{"file":"pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go","line":51,"severity":"high","category":"bug","title":"Async legacy writes derive their context from the request context, which is cancelled when the handler returns","body":"Each goroutine (Create l.51, Delete l.110, Update l.135, DeleteCollection l.163) does `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)` on the request-scoped `ctx`. The API server cancels that context as soon as the HTTP handler returns, and the goroutine intentionally outlives the handler. The legacy write will therefore usually run with an already-cancelled context and fail or abort. The legacy store silently drifts from unified storage, which is the opposite of the 'safe measure' described in the PR. Use `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` (or a fresh background context carrying the logger) as the parent of the timeout context."},
{"file":"pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go","line":59,"severity":"medium","category":"bug","title":"Legacy write errors are no longer logged; failures in the goroutines are invisible","body":"The old code logged legacy failures (`unable to create object in legacy storage`, `could not delete from legacy store`, `could not update object in legacy store`). In the new goroutines the error is only used as a boolean for `recordLegacyDuration`, and never logged. Combined with the cancelled-context problem, legacy writes can fail with no log trace. That makes legacy/unified divergence hard to diagnose. Log the error inside each goroutine."},
{"file":"pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go","line":45,"severity":"medium","category":"bug","title":"Storage create failure is recorded as a legacy duration metric","body":"When `d.Storage.Create` fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)`. The failure came from unified storage, so it should be `recordStorageDuration(true, ...)`. As written, storage errors pollute the legacy error and latency series and the storage error series stays empty, which misleads dashboards and alerts during the mode 3 rollout."},
{"file":"pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go","line":129,"severity":"medium","category":"bug","title":"Storage update failure is recorded with recordLegacyDuration","body":"On `d.Storage.Update` error the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` with `startStorage`. This is the same copy/paste mistake as in Create. Unified-storage failures get attributed to the legacy metric. It should be `recordStorageDuration`."},
{"file":"pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go","line":106,"severity":"low","category":"bug","title":"Delete success metric uses `name` instead of `options.Kind` as the label","body":"Every other metric call passes `options.Kind` as the name/kind label. The success path of Delete passes `name` (the object name). This produces one label value per deleted object, which is a high-cardinality metric. It also splits the success series from the error series, which uses `options.Kind`. It should be `options.Kind`."},
{"file":"pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go","line":166,"severity":"medium","category":"bug","title":"Legacy DeleteCollection duration is recorded as a storage duration","body":"Inside the goroutine that calls `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection`, the result is recorded with `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ..., startLegacy)`. It should be `recordLegacyDuration`. Legacy latency and errors are attributed to the storage metrics, which double-counts storage and hides legacy failures."},
{"file":"pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go","line":97,"severity":"low","category":"bug","title":"Delete puts the un-annotated logger into the context instead of the enriched one","body":"`ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` discards the per-call `log` (name, kind, method) that was just built. All other methods use `klog.NewContext(ctx, log)`. Logs emitted downstream from the context lose the request attributes. It should use `log`."},
{"file":"pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go","line":139,"severity":"medium","category":"data","title":"Legacy update re-applies the original objInfo instead of the object written to storage","body":"The previous implementation wrapped the result in `updateWrapper` so legacy stored exactly the object that unified storage persisted. Now the goroutine calls `d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` with the raw `objInfo`. For patch/apply requests the update is re-computed against whatever legacy currently holds, and it runs after the response has gone out. If legacy state differs, or `forceAllowCreate` or validation behave differently, legacy ends up with a different object than unified storage. This divergence is not detected or logged."},
{"file":"pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3.go","line":55,"severity":"medium","category":"concurrency","title":"Same `obj` is handed to the async legacy Create while the handler may still serialize `created`","body":"The goroutine passes the original `obj` to `d.Legacy.Create` after `Storage.Create` has returned. `created` is often the same pointer or shares its internals with `obj`. Legacy Create commonly mutates the object (UID, resourceVersion, metadata), while the request handler concurrently encodes `created` for the response. This is an unsynchronized read/write on the same object (a data race). Deep-copy the object before launching the goroutine."},
{"file":"pkg/apiserver/rest/dualwriter_mode3_test.go","line":63,"severity":"medium","category":"test_gap","title":"Unit tests never verify the asynchronous legacy writes","body":"The Mode 3 tests only check the return values from unified storage. The legacy write runs in an un-awaited goroutine, and nothing asserts that Legacy.Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection are called, or that the legacy error path is handled. Because legacy and storage mocks share one `mock.Mock`, the legacy goroutine silently consumes the storage expectation. The tests would still pass if the goroutines were removed, or if they received a cancelled context. The tests need a sync mechanism (channel/WaitGroup or `Eventually`) with `AssertCalled`, and separate legacy and storage mocks."},
{"file":"pkg/tests/apis/playlist/playlist_test.go","line":132,"severity":"medium","category":"test_gap","title":"Mode 3 integration runs reuse tests that read legacy immediately after k8s writes, but legacy writes are async","body":"`doPlaylistTests` creates, updates and deletes through the k8s API and then immediately reads the legacy `/api/playlists` endpoint (`searchResponse`, `getFromBothAPIs`). In mode 3 the legacy write is fire-and-forget, so those assertions race with the goroutine. They are flaky, or they pass only by accident of timing. Mode 3 needs its own assertions, or the legacy checks should poll with `Eventually`."},
{"file":"go.work.sum","line":405,"severity":"low","category":"style","title":"Unrelated and duplicated go.work.sum entries","body":"The go.work.sum changes (azure sdk, otel, alertmanager, genproto, etc.) are unrelated to the dual-writer change. The line for `github.com/grafana/grafana/pkg/apimachinery v0.0.0-20240701135906-559738ce6ae1/go.mod` is added twice, directly under the identical existing line. This looks like an accidental `go work sync` artifact and should be dropped from the PR."}
]}

findings.title: Async legacy writes derive their context from the request context, which is cancelled when the handler returns
findings.body: Each goroutine (Create l.51, Delete l.110, Update l.135, DeleteCollection l.163) does `context.WithTimeoutCause(ctx, ...)` on the request-scoped `ctx`. The API server cancels that context as soon as the HTTP handler returns, and the goroutine intentionally outlives the handler. The legacy write will therefore usually run with an already-cancelled context and fail or abort. The legacy store silently drifts from unified storage, which is the opposite of the 'safe measure' described in the PR. Use `context.WithoutCancel(ctx)` (or a fresh background context carrying the logger) as the parent of the timeout context.

findings.title: Legacy write errors are no longer logged; failures in the goroutines are invisible
findings.body: The old code logged legacy failures (`unable to create object in legacy storage`, `could not delete from legacy store`, `could not update object in legacy store`). In the new goroutines the error is only used as a boolean for `recordLegacyDuration`, and never logged. Combined with the cancelled-context problem, legacy writes can fail with no log trace. That makes legacy/unified divergence hard to diagnose. Log the error inside each goroutine.

findings.title: Storage create failure is recorded as a legacy duration metric
findings.body: When `d.Storage.Create` fails, the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)`. The failure came from unified storage, so it should be `recordStorageDuration(true, ...)`. As written, storage errors pollute the legacy error and latency series and the storage error series stays empty, which misleads dashboards and alerts during the mode 3 rollout.

findings.title: Storage update failure is recorded with recordLegacyDuration
findings.body: On `d.Storage.Update` error the code calls `d.recordLegacyDuration(true, ...)` with `startStorage`. This is the same copy/paste mistake as in Create. Unified-storage failures get attributed to the legacy metric. It should be `recordStorageDuration`.

findings.title: Delete success metric uses `name` instead of `options.Kind` as the label
findings.body: Every other metric call passes `options.Kind` as the name/kind label. The success path of Delete passes `name` (the object name). This produces one label value per deleted object, which is a high-cardinality metric. It also splits the success series from the error series, which uses `options.Kind`. It should be `options.Kind`.

findings.title: Legacy DeleteCollection duration is recorded as a storage duration
findings.body: Inside the goroutine that calls `d.Legacy.DeleteCollection`, the result is recorded with `d.recordStorageDuration(err != nil, ..., startLegacy)`. It should be `recordLegacyDuration`. Legacy latency and errors are attributed to the storage metrics, which double-counts storage and hides legacy failures.

findings.title: Delete puts the un-annotated logger into the context instead of the enriched one
findings.body: `ctx = klog.NewContext(ctx, d.Log)` discards the per-call `log` (name, kind, method) that was just built. All other methods use `klog.NewContext(ctx, log)`. Logs emitted downstream from the context lose the request attributes. It should use `log`.

findings.title: Legacy update re-applies the original objInfo instead of the object written to storage
findings.body: The previous implementation wrapped the result in `updateWrapper` so legacy stored exactly the object that unified storage persisted. Now the goroutine calls `d.Legacy.Update(ctx, name, objInfo, ...)` with the raw `objInfo`. For patch/apply requests the update is re-computed against whatever legacy currently holds, and it runs after the response has gone out. If legacy state differs, or `forceAllowCreate` or validation behave differently, legacy ends up with a different object than unified storage. This divergence is not detected or logged.

findings.title: Same `obj` is handed to the async legacy Create while the handler may still serialize `created`
findings.body: The goroutine passes the original `obj` to `d.Legacy.Create` after `Storage.Create` has returned. `created` is often the same pointer or shares its internals with `obj`. Legacy Create commonly mutates the object (UID, resourceVersion, metadata), while the request handler concurrently encodes `created` for the response. This is an unsynchronized read/write on the same object (a data race). Deep-copy the object before launching the goroutine.

findings.title: Unit tests never verify the asynchronous legacy writes
findings.body: The Mode 3 tests only check the return values from unified storage. The legacy write runs in an un-awaited goroutine, and nothing asserts that Legacy.Create/Update/Delete/DeleteCollection are called, or that the legacy error path is handled. Because legacy and storage mocks share one `mock.Mock`, the legacy goroutine silently consumes the storage expectation. The tests would still pass if the goroutines were removed, or if they received a cancelled context. The tests need a sync mechanism (channel/WaitGroup or `Eventually`) with `AssertCalled`, and separate legacy and storage mocks.

findings.title: Mode 3 integration runs reuse tests that read legacy immediately after k8s writes, but legacy writes are async
findings.body: `doPlaylistTests` creates, updates and deletes through the k8s API and then immediately reads the legacy `/api/playlists` endpoint (`searchResponse`, `getFromBothAPIs`). In mode 3 the legacy write is fire-and-forget, so those assertions race with the goroutine. They are flaky, or they pass only by accident of timing. Mode 3 needs its own assertions, or the legacy checks should poll with `Eventually`.

findings.title: Unrelated and duplicated go.work.sum entries
findings.body: The go.work.sum changes (azure sdk, otel, alertmanager, genproto, etc.) are unrelated to the dual-writer change. The line for `github.com/grafana/grafana/pkg/apimachinery v0.0.0-20240701135906-559738ce6ae1/go.mod` is added twice, directly under the identical existing line. This looks like an accidental `go work sync` artifact and should be dropped from the PR.
